attacks.claim: The plan says the backfill runs on a low-priority Celery queue so publishing is never delayed, but it runs on the same two worker nodes (8 worker slots total) that process publishing tasks. A separate queue does not give priority by itself, so during the 01:00–06:00 window the backfill can occupy every slot and delay publish-time `make_display_jpeg` and `make_responsive_set` runs. No dedicated worker pool, concurrency cap, or queue-isolation mechanism is described.
attacks.evidence: "Two existing worker nodes × 4 workers ≈ 9.7 h, run over two nights (01:00–06:00) on a separate low-priority Celery queue, so publishing tasks are never delayed."
